_meta.what: Zoning declarations for the UPG-100 list: the facts about this list's zoning that a gate cannot infer and a reader cannot guess from the data.
_meta.why: check-zoning-declared.mjs asserts the ACTUAL zoning against these DECLARATIONS. Without them a gate can only test self-consistency, which is satisfied by a zoning that silently dropped groups.
_meta.how_to_use: A new project list ships its own <id>.json beside this one. Copy the shape, not the values.

bloc_zones._why: Zones that partition by AFFINITY or LANGUAGE rather than geography. Their members ALSO belong to a geographic zone, so they are exempt from the one-geographic-zone rule. legend-tree.js:151 records the deaf case as design-approved (slice 08): per-zone equality holds; only a naive GLOBAL sum over-counts.

expected_orphans._why: Groups in the list that belong to NO zone. An empty list here means 'every group must be zoned'. A gate cannot tell a deliberate exclusion from a silent drop; only this declaration can.
expected_orphans._status: PENDING A PRODUCT DECISION — these 11 are TODAY'S ACTUAL orphans, recorded so the gate is green on arrival and any NEW orphan fails. They are all Japan / China / Mongolia and are plausibly deliberate (asia-china-tibet-autonomous-region is labelled 'Mainland China + Mongolia' and carries only 43 groups), but nobody has said so. In the product-decisions digest; do NOT change the memberships to make this list shorter.

known_geographic_overlaps._why: Groups that DO sit in two geographic zones, declared so the gate fails on a NEW overlap rather than on these. Not an endorsement — see _status.
known_geographic_overlaps._status: PENDING A PRODUCT DECISION — uncovered-scatter is country_codes AND,CCK,GUF,USA ('Scattered / Diaspora'), so it overlaps the regional zones it scatters across. Either a scatter zone is a THIRD partition (like a bloc) or these two memberships are wrong. In the product-decisions digest; do NOT change either membership. ⚠ deaf-cocos-islanders was MISSED by my own hand analysis and found by this gate: I had filtered out every A017 group as 'the design-approved deaf double-count', but its TWO GEOGRAPHIC claims (CCK is in both zones' country lists) are a SEPARATE fact from its bloc membership. Conflating them is exactly what the bloc/geographic split in A2 exists to prevent, and the gate got it right where I did not — which is the best argument for the gate existing.

page_budget._why: Groups per printed page, from packet-render's PER_PAGE. A zone larger than max_groups is not an error — it just prints more sheets — but a zone WILDLY larger is usually a selector that matched too much, which is how the wagf and deaf selector bugs looked before they were found.
